The following patch updates the way SELinux classifies and handles IP
based protocols.
Currently
column2: IP sockets are classified by SELinux as being either TCP

column1: or 'Raw'
column2: the latter being a default for IP socket that is not TCP or UDP.

column1: The classification code is out of date and uses only the socket type
parameter to socket(2) to determine the class of IP socket.  So
socket created with SOCK_STREAM will be classified by SELinux as TCP
SOCK_DGRAM as UDP.  Also
column2: other socket types such as SOCK_SEQPACKET and

column1: SOCK_DCCP are currently ignored by SELinux
generic sockets
column2: which means they don't even get basic IP level checking.

column1: This patch changes the SELinux IP socket classification logic
only an IPPROTO_IP protocol value passed to socket(2) classify the socket
as TCP or UDP.  The patch also drops the check for SOCK_RAW and converts
it into a default
column2: so that socket types like SOCK_DCCP and SOCK_SEQPACKET

column1: are classified as SECCLASS_RAWIP_SOCKET (instead of generic sockets).
Note that protocol-specific support for SCTP
here
column2: we're just getting these protocols checked at the IP layer.

column1: This fixes a reported problem where SCTP sockets were being recognized as
generic SELinux sockets yet still being passed in one case to an IP level
check
column2: which then fails for generic sockets.

column1: It will also fix bugs where any SOCK_STREAM socket is classified as TCP or
any SOCK_DGRAM socket is classified as UDP.
This patch also unifies the way IP sockets classes are determined in
selinux_socket_bind()
column2: so we use the already calculated value instead of

column1: trying to recalculate it.
